units.zh: 範延光，字子環，鄴郡臨漳人也。
units.en: Fan Yanguang, whose courtesy name was Zihuan, came from Linzhang in Ye Commandery.
units.literal: Fan Yanguang, courtesy name Zihuan, was a native of Linzhang in Ye Commandery.

units.zh: 少隸於郡牙，唐明宗牧相州，收為親校。
units.en: As a young man he served in the commandery headquarters. When Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang was posted to Xiangzhou, he recruited Fan as a personal guard.
units.literal: In youth he served under the commandant of the commandery; when Tang Emperor Mingzong governed Xiangzhou, he took him in as a personal attendant.

units.zh: 同光中，明宗下鄆州，梁兵屯楊劉口以扼之，先鋒將康延孝潛使人送款於明宗。
units.en: During the Tongguang reign, Mingzong marched on Yanzhou. Liang forces camped at Yangliu Ford to block his advance, while the vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao secretly sent envoys to pledge allegiance to Mingzong.
units.literal: In the Tongguang era, Mingzong advanced on Yanzhou; Liang troops encamped at Yangliu Ford to block him, and the vanguard general Kang Yanxiao secretly sent men to offer submission to Mingzong.

units.zh: 明宗欲使人達機事於莊宗，方難其選，延光請行，遂以蠟書授之。
units.en: Mingzong needed someone to carry urgent intelligence to Zhuangzong but could not settle on a courier. Yanguang volunteered for the mission and was given a dispatch sealed in wax.
units.literal: Mingzong wished to send someone to convey urgent business to Zhuangzong and was just finding it hard to choose; Yanguang asked to go, and he was entrusted with a letter sealed in wax.

units.zh: 延光既至，奏莊宗曰：「楊劉渡控扼已定，未可圖也。
units.en: Once he arrived, Yanguang reported to Zhuangzong: "The Yangliu crossing is already firmly held. It cannot be taken by force.
units.literal: When Yanguang arrived, he reported to Zhuangzong, saying, "The Yangliu crossing is already firmly held and cannot be taken.

units.zh: 請築壘馬家口，以通汶陽之路。」
units.en: I ask that we build a fort at Majiakou to open a route toward Wenyang."
units.literal: I ask that a fort be built at Majiakou to open the road to Wenyang."

units.zh: 莊宗從之，復遣歸鄆州。
units.en: Zhuangzong agreed and sent him back to Yanzhou.
units.literal: Zhuangzong followed this advice and sent him back to Yanzhou.

units.zh: 俄而梁將王彥章攻馬家口所築新壘，明宗恐城中不備，又遣間行告莊宗，請益兵。
units.en: Soon afterward the Liang general Wang Yanzhang attacked the new fort at Majiakou. Fearing the city was unprepared, Mingzong again sent a secret courier to Zhuangzong asking for more troops.
units.literal: Before long the Liang general Wang Yanzhang attacked the new fort built at Majiakou; Mingzong feared the city was unprepared and again sent a secret messenger to inform Zhuangzong and request reinforcements.

units.zh: 中夜至河上，為梁兵所獲，送夷門下獄，榜笞數百，威以白刃，終不泄其事。
units.en: He reached the river in the middle of the night and was captured by Liang troops. They sent him to prison at Yimen, flogged him hundreds of times, and threatened him with drawn swords, but he never revealed what he knew.
units.literal: In the middle of the night he reached the river and was seized by Liang troops; he was sent to prison at Yimen, flogged hundreds of times, and threatened with naked blades, yet in the end he would not reveal the affair.

units.zh: 復為獄吏所護，在獄半年，不復理問。
units.en: The prison officials shielded him as well, and for half a year he was left in custody without further questioning.
units.literal: He was again protected by the prison officials; he remained in prison half a year without further interrogation.

units.zh: 及莊宗將至汴城，獄吏即去其桎梏，拜謝而出之，乃見於路側。
units.en: When Zhuangzong was approaching Bian, the jailers removed his shackles, bowed in gratitude, and released him. He was found waiting by the roadside.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong was about to reach Bian city, the prison officials at once removed his fetters, bowed in thanks, and released him; he was then seen by the roadside.

units.zh: 莊宗喜，授銀青光祿大夫、檢校工部尚書。
units.en: Zhuangzong was delighted and appointed him Silver-and-Azure Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was pleased and appointed him Silver-and-Azure Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 明宗登極，擢為宣徽使。
units.en: After Mingzong took the throne, he was promoted to Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
units.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 與霍彥威平青州王公儼，遷檢校司徒。
units.en: Together with Huo Yanwei he suppressed Wang Gongyan in Qingzhou and was promoted to acting Grand Mentor.
units.literal: Together with Huo Yanwei he pacified Wang Gongyan of Qingzhou and was transferred to acting Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 明宗之幸夷門也，至滎陽，聞朱守殷拒命，延光曰：「若不急攻，賊堅矣。
units.en: On Mingzong's visit to Yimen, when he reached Xingyang he learned that Zhu Shouyin was in rebellion. Yanguang said, "If we do not strike at once, the rebels will dig in.
units.literal: When Mingzong visited Yimen and reached Xingyang, he heard that Zhu Shouyin was defying orders; Yanguang said, "If we do not attack quickly, the rebels will harden.

units.zh: 請騎兵五百，臣先赴之，則人心必駭。」
units.en: Give me five hundred cavalry and let me ride ahead. That alone will terrify them."
units.literal: I ask for five hundred cavalry; if your servant goes ahead, the people's hearts will surely be struck with fear."

units.zh: 明宗從其請。
units.en: Mingzong granted the request.
units.literal: Mingzong granted his request.

units.zh: 延光自酉時至夜央，馳二百餘里，奄至城下，與賊交鬥。
units.en: From dusk until midnight Yanguang rode more than two hundred li and suddenly appeared beneath the walls, where he clashed with the rebels.
units.literal: From the hour of you until the middle of the night Yanguang galloped more than two hundred li and suddenly arrived below the walls, fighting the rebels.

units.zh: 翌日，守陴者望見乘輿，乃相率開門，延光先入，與賊巷戰，至厚載門，盡殲其黨，明宗喜之。
units.en: The next day the defenders on the walls saw the imperial carriage and opened the gates together. Yanguang entered first and fought the rebels street by street as far as Houzai Gate, wiping out their party. Mingzong was greatly pleased.
units.literal: The next day the defenders on the battlements saw the imperial carriage and all together opened the gates; Yanguang entered first and fought the rebels in the lanes as far as Houzai Gate, annihilating their faction; Mingzong was pleased.

units.zh: 明年，遷樞密使，權知鎮州軍府事，尋正授節旄，加檢校太保。
units.en: The following year he was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting administrator of Zhenzhou. Soon he received a full commission as military governor and the additional title of acting Grand Guardian.
units.literal: The next year he was transferred to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, acting administrator of the Zhenzhou military government; soon he received the full commission as military governor and was given the additional title of acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 長興中，以安重誨得罪，再入為樞密使，加同平章事。
units.en: During the Changxing reign, after An Chonghui fell from power, he returned to the post of Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was made Associate Grand Councillor.
units.literal: In the Changxing era, because An Chonghui fell from favor, he again entered office as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was given the title of Associate Grand Councillor.

units.zh: 既而以秦王從榮不軌，恐及其禍，屢請外任，明宗久之方許，遂出鎮常山。
units.en: When Congrong, Prince of Qin, plotted rebellion, Yanguang feared he would be swept up in the fallout and repeatedly asked for a provincial post. Mingzong delayed a long time before agreeing, and he was sent to govern Changshan.
units.literal: Then because Congrong, Prince of Qin, was disloyal, fearing he would be implicated in the disaster, he repeatedly asked for an outside post; only after a long time did Mingzong consent, and he went out to govern Changshan.

units.zh: 清泰中，復詔為樞密使，未幾，出為汴州節度使。
units.en: During the Qingtai reign he was recalled as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but before long he was posted out as military governor of Bianzhou.
units.literal: In the Qingtai era he was again ordered to be Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; before long he went out as military governor of Bianzhou.

units.zh: 會魏府屯將張令昭逐其帥劉延皓，據城以叛，唐末帝命延光討而平之，遂授鄴都留守，加檢校太師、兼中書令。
units.en: When the Weifu garrison officer Zhang Lingzhao expelled his commander Liu Yanhao and seized the city in rebellion, the last Tang emperor ordered Yanguang to suppress him. After the campaign he was made defender of the Ye capital with the additional titles of acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: It happened that the garrison officer Zhang Lingzhao of Weifu drove out his commander Liu Yanhao, seized the city, and rebelled; the last Tang emperor ordered Yanguang to attack and pacify him, then appointed him defender of the Ye capital, with the additional titles of acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 門下有術士張生者，自雲妙通術數，當延光微時，言將來必為將相，延光既貴，酷信其言。
units.en: Among his retainers was a diviner named Zhang who claimed mastery of occult arts. When Yanguang was still obscure, Zhang predicted that he would one day become a general or chief minister. Once Yanguang had risen high, he trusted Zhang completely.
units.literal: Among his retainers was a practitioner of the arts named Zhang, who claimed to be skilled in divination and numerology; when Yanguang was still obscure he said that in the future he would surely become a general or minister, and once Yanguang had risen high he believed his words intensely.

units.zh: 歷數鎮，嘗館於上舍，延光謂之曰：「余夢大蛇，自臍入腹，半而掣去之，是何祥也？」
units.en: During several provincial postings he once lodged Zhang in his best guest quarters. Yanguang told him, "I dreamed of a great serpent entering my belly through the navel and being pulled out halfway. What does this portend?"
units.literal: Through several governorships he once lodged Zhang in the upper guesthouse; Yanguang said to him, "I dreamed of a great serpent entering my belly from the navel and being pulled out halfway—what omen is this?"

units.zh: 張生曰：「蛇者龍也，入腹為帝王之兆明矣。」
units.en: Zhang replied, "A serpent is a dragon in disguise. For it to enter your belly is plainly an omen that you will become emperor."
units.literal: Zhang said, "A serpent is a dragon; entering the belly is plainly an omen of becoming emperor."

units.zh: 延光自是稍萌僭竊之意。
units.en: From that time Yanguang began to entertain thoughts of usurpation.
units.literal: From this Yanguang gradually began to harbor thoughts of usurpation.

units.zh: 及高祖建義於太原，唐末帝遣延光以本部二萬屯遼州，與趙延壽掎角合勢，及延壽兵敗，延光促還，故心不自安。
units.en: When Emperor Gaozu of Later Jin raised his banner at Taiyuan, the last Tang emperor sent Yanguang with twenty thousand troops from his command to camp at Liaozhou and coordinate with Zhao Yanshou in a pincer movement. After Yanshou was defeated, Yanguang was ordered back, and he grew uneasy.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor raised the righteous cause at Taiyuan, the last Tang emperor sent Yanguang with twenty thousand men of his command to encamp at Liaozhou and coordinate with Zhao Yanshou in pincer fashion; when Yanshou's army was defeated, Yanguang was urged to return, and therefore his heart was not at ease.

units.zh: 高祖入洛，尋封臨清王，以寬其反側。
units.en: After Gaozu entered Luoyang, he soon enfeoffed Yanguang as Prince of Linqing to calm his restless mind.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor entered Luoyang, he soon enfeoffed him as Prince of Linqing to ease his disloyal restlessness.

units.zh: 後延光擅殺齊州防禦使秘瓊，而聚兵部下，復收部內刺史入城，高祖甚疑之，乃東幸夷門。
units.en: Later Yanguang executed Mi Qiong, defense commissioner of Qizhou, on his own authority, gathered troops under his command, and summoned the prefects within his circuit into the city. Gaozu grew deeply suspicious and traveled east to Yimen.
units.literal: Later Yanguang on his own authority killed Mi Qiong, defense commissioner of Qizhou, gathered troops under his command, and again summoned the prefects within his circuit into the city; the High Ancestor was greatly suspicious and therefore went east to visit Yimen.

units.zh: 時延光有牙校孫銳者，與延光有鄉曲之舊，軍機民政，一以委焉。
units.en: At that time Yanguang had a staff officer named Sun Rui, an old fellow townsman to whom he entrusted all military and civil affairs.
units.literal: At that time Yanguang had a staff officer named Sun Rui who shared old ties of native place with him; military affairs and civil administration were wholly entrusted to him.

units.zh: 故魏博六州之賦，無半錢上供，符奏之間，有不如意者，銳即對延光毀之，其兇戾也如此。
units.en: Not half a coin of tax from the six Weibo prefectures reached the court. Whenever an official report displeased him, Rui would slander the author to Yanguang on the spot. That was how brutal he was.
units.literal: Thus of the taxes of the six prefectures of Weibo not half a coin was sent up; whenever something in official correspondence was not to his liking, Rui would at once slander the person before Yanguang—such was his ferocity.

units.zh: 初，朝廷遣使封延光為臨清王，因會僚屬，延光暴得疾，伏枕經旬，銳乃密惑群小，召澶州刺史馮暉等，以不臣之謀逼於延光，延光亦惑於術者，因而聽之。
units.en: When the court first sent envoys to enfeoff him as Prince of Linqing, he fell suddenly ill while meeting his staff and was bedridden for ten days. Rui secretly stirred up the lesser officers, summoned Cao Prefecture prefect Feng Hui and others, and pressed a treasonous plot on Yanguang, who was also swayed by the diviner and went along.
units.literal: At first the court sent envoys to enfeoff Yanguang as Prince of Linqing; when he met with his subordinates he suddenly fell ill and lay on his pillow for ten days; Rui then secretly misled the lesser men, summoned Feng Hui, prefect of Cao Prefecture, and others, and pressed disloyal plans on Yanguang; Yanguang was also deluded by the diviner and therefore listened.

units.zh: 天福二年夏六月，遣銳與暉將步騎二萬，南抵黎陽。
units.en: In the sixth month of summer in the second year of Tianfu he sent Rui and Feng Hui south with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry as far as Liyang.
units.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the second year of Tianfu he sent Rui and Hui to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry south to Liyang.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：延光以馮暉為都部署，以孫銳為兵馬都監。）〉
units.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 records that Yanguang made Feng Hui overall commander and Sun Rui commander of troops and horses.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: Yanguang made Feng Hui overall commander and Sun Rui commander of troops and horses.)〉

units.zh: 時銳以女妓十餘輩從之，擁蓋操扇，必歌吹而後食，將士煩熱，睹之解體，尋為王師所敗，賊眾退還鄴城。
units.en: Sun Rui traveled with more than ten female entertainers, shaded by parasols and waving fans, and would not eat until musicians had performed. The troops, sweltering in the heat, lost all fighting spirit at the sight. Soon the imperial army defeated them and the rebels fell back to Ye.
units.literal: At that time Rui was accompanied by more than ten female entertainers; shaded by parasols and wielding fans, he would not eat until there had been song and music; the officers and soldiers, oppressed by heat, saw this and lost heart; soon they were defeated by the imperial army and the rebel host withdrew to Ye city.

units.zh: 高祖繼遣楊光遠討之，延光知事不濟，乃殺孫銳以歸其罪，發人賫表待罪，且邀姑息，高祖不許。
units.en: Gaozu then sent Yang Guangyuan against him. Seeing that the cause was lost, Yanguang killed Sun Rui to shift the blame, sent a memorial accepting guilt, and asked for leniency. Gaozu refused.
units.literal: The High Ancestor then sent Yang Guangyuan to attack him; Yanguang knew the affair would not succeed, so he killed Sun Rui to assign him the blame, sent men bearing a memorial to await punishment, and also sought lenient treatment; the High Ancestor would not agree.

units.zh: 及經歲受圍，城中饑窘，高祖以師老民勞，思解其役，遣謁者入謂之曰：「卿既危蹙，破在旦夕。
units.en: After a year under siege the city was starving. Gaozu, weary of the campaign and its toll on the people, wished to end it. He sent an envoy who said, "You are already cornered. Defeat will come within days.
units.literal: After a year under siege the city was hungry and distressed; the High Ancestor, because the army was weary and the people worn, wished to end the campaign and sent an envoy in to say, "You are already in desperate straits; defeat is at hand by dawn.

units.zh: 能返掌轉規，改節歸我，我當以大藩處之。
units.en: If you turn back now, change your allegiance, and submit to me, I will give you a major frontier command.
units.literal: If you can turn the palm and change course, alter your loyalty and return to me, I shall place you in a great frontier post.

units.zh: 如降而殺之，則何以享國？
units.en: If I killed you after you surrendered, how could I hold the realm in honor?
units.literal: If I killed you after you surrendered, how could I enjoy the realm?

units.zh: 明明白日，可質是言。」
units.en: In broad daylight you may take this as my pledge."
units.literal: In broad daylight this word may be taken as pledge."

units.zh: 因賜鐵券，改封高平郡王，移鎮太平。
units.en: He granted an iron certificate of mercy, changed his title to Prince of Gaoping, and promised to transfer him to Taiping.
units.literal: He therefore granted an iron certificate, changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Gaoping, and transferred him to govern Taiping.

units.zh: 延光謂門人李式曰：「主上敦信明義，言無不踐，許以不死，則不死矣。」
units.en: Yanguang told his follower Li Shi, "Our lord is sincere and keeps his word. If he promises I shall not die, then I shall not die."
units.literal: Yanguang said to his follower Li Shi, "Our lord is sincere in faith and clear in righteousness; his words are never unfulfilled; if he promises that I shall not die, then I shall not die."

units.zh: 因撤去守備，
units.en: He then removed the defenses,
units.literal: He therefore removed the defenses,

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：延光猶遷延未決，宣徽南院使劉處讓復入諭之，延光意乃決。）〉
units.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 adds that Yanguang still hesitated until Liu Churang, commissioner of the southern bureau of the Palace Secretariat, entered again to persuade him, whereupon he made up his mind.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》: Yanguang still hesitated and had not decided; Liu Churang, commissioner of the southern bureau of the Palace Secretariat, again entered to instruct him, and only then did Yanguang's mind become settled.)〉

units.zh: 素服請降。
units.en: and came out in plain dress to surrender.
units.literal: and in plain dress asked to surrender.

units.zh: 及赴汶上，逾月入覲。
units.en: After he went to Wen Shang, he had an audience more than a month later.
units.literal: When he went to Wen Shang, after more than a month he had an audience.

units.zh: 尋表請罷免，高祖再三答諭方允，制以延光為太子太師致仕。
units.en: Soon he asked to retire from office. Gaozu repeatedly urged him to stay before consenting and appointed him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in retirement.
units.literal: Soon he memorialized asking to be dismissed; only after the High Ancestor repeatedly answered and instructed him did he consent, and by edict Yanguang was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in retirement.

units.zh: 居闕下期歲，高祖每召賜飲宴，待之與群臣無間。
units.en: He remained at court for nearly a year. Gaozu often summoned him to banquets and treated him no differently from the other ministers.
units.literal: He dwelt at the capital nearly a year; the High Ancestor often summoned him to banquets and treated him no differently from the other ministers.

units.zh: 一日，從容上奏，願就河陽私邸，以便頤養，高祖許之。
units.en: One day he calmly asked permission to retire to his private residence at Heyang for his health. Gaozu agreed.
units.literal: One day he calmly submitted that he wished to go to his private residence at Heyang for ease in nourishing his years; the High Ancestor granted it.

units.zh: 延光攜妻子輦奇貨從焉，每過郡邑，多為關吏所糾。
units.en: Yanguang took his wife, children, and carts laden with rare goods. At nearly every post along the way barrier officials challenged him.
units.literal: Yanguang took his wife and children and loaded rare goods on carts to go with him; whenever he passed through a commandery or district he was often challenged by barrier officials.

units.zh: 時楊光遠居守洛下，兼領孟、懷，既利其財，復漸測朝廷密旨，遂奏云：「延光國之奸臣，若不羈縻，必北出塞，南入吳，請召令西都居止。」
units.en: Yang Guangyuan was then left to guard Luoyang while also holding Meng and Huai. Coveting Yanguang's wealth and sensing the court's secret intent, he memorialized: "Yanguang is a traitor to the state. Unless he is restrained he will flee north beyond the frontier or south into Wu. I ask that he be summoned to the western capital."
units.literal: At that time Yang Guangyuan was left to guard Luoyang and also held Meng and Huai; he both coveted Yanguang's wealth and gradually inferred the court's secret intent, and therefore memorialized, "Yanguang is a traitor to the state; if he is not restrained he will surely go north beyond the passes or south into Wu—I ask that he be summoned to dwell in the western capital."

units.zh: 高祖允之。
units.en: Gaozu agreed.
units.literal: The High Ancestor granted it.

units.zh: 光遠使其子承勛以兵環其第，逼令自裁。
units.en: Guangyuan sent his son Chengxun with troops to surround the residence and forced Yanguang to kill himself.
units.literal: Guangyuan had his son Chengxun surround his residence with troops and forced him to take his own life.

units.zh: 延光曰：「明天子在上，賜金書許我不死，爾之父子何得脅制如此？」
units.en: Yanguang said, "The enlightened Son of Heaven granted me a golden document promising I would not die. How dare you father and son coerce me like this?"
units.literal: Yanguang said, "The enlightened Son of Heaven is above; he granted a golden document promising that I would not die—how can you father and son coerce me thus?"

units.zh: 明旦，則以白刃驅之，令上馬之浮橋，排於水中。
units.en: At dawn the next day they drove him at sword point onto a pontoon bridge, forced him onto a horse, and pushed him into the river.
units.literal: At dawn the next day they drove him with naked blades, made him mount a horse onto the pontoon bridge, and pushed him into the water.

units.zh: 光遠紿奏云：「延光投河自溺而死。」
units.en: Guangyuan falsely reported, "Yanguang threw himself into the river and drowned."
units.literal: Guangyuan falsely reported, "Yanguang threw himself into the river and drowned."

units.zh: 水運軍使曹千獲其屍於郡東繆家灘。
units.en: Cao Qian, commissioner of water transport troops, recovered his body at Miaojia Shoal east of the prefecture.
units.literal: Cao Qian, commissioner of water transport troops, recovered his corpse at Miaojia Shoal east of the prefecture.

units.zh: 高祖聞之，輟朝二日，詔許歸葬於鄴，仍贈太師。
units.en: When Gaozu heard of it he suspended court for two days, permitted burial at Ye, and posthumously granted him the title of Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor heard of it he suspended court for two days and ordered that burial be permitted at Ye, still posthumously granting him Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 延光初為近臣，及領重鎮，禮賢接士，動皆由禮，故甚獲當時之譽。
units.en: In his early career as a court favorite and later as governor of a major command, Yanguang honored worthy men and received scholars with courtesy. He won great praise in his day.
units.literal: At first, as a close minister and then as holder of a weighty frontier post, Yanguang honored the worthy and received scholars; his every act followed ritual, and therefore he won great praise in his day.

units.zh: 洎鎮常山日，以部將梁漢塘獲王都名馬，入罪而取之；
units.en: When he governed Changshan he framed his subordinate Liang Hantang for obtaining a famous horse belonging to Wang Du and seized it;
units.literal: When he governed Changshan, because his subordinate Liang Hantang had obtained a famous horse of Wang Du, he entered a charge against him and took it;

units.zh: 在魏州日，以齊州防禦使秘瓊獲董溫琪珠金妓妾，及經其境，復害而奪之。
units.en: at Weizhou he killed Qizhou defense commissioner Mi Qiong, who had seized Dong Wenqi's pearls, gold, and courtesans, when Mi passed through his territory and took them for himself.
units.literal: when he was at Weizhou, because the defense commissioner of Qizhou, Mi Qiong, had obtained the pearls, gold, and courtesans of Dong Wenqi, when Mi passed through his territory he again killed him and seized them.

units.zh: 物議由是減之。
units.en: Public opinion turned against him.
units.literal: Public opinion therefore diminished him.

units.zh: 及懼罪以謀叛，復忍恥以偷生，不能引決，遂至強死，何非夫之甚也！
units.en: When he feared punishment he rebelled, then endured shame to cling to life rather than take his own. He was forced to die in the end. How far he fell short of what a man should be!
units.literal: When he feared punishment and plotted rebellion, then endured shame to cling to life and could not resolve to die, and finally came to forced death—how greatly he failed the measure of a man!

units.zh: 張從賓，未詳何許人也。
units.en: Zhang Congbin's place of origin is not recorded.
units.literal: Zhang Congbin—his native place is not clearly known.

units.zh: 始事唐莊宗為小校，從戰有功。
units.en: He first served Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang as a junior officer and distinguished himself in battle.
units.literal: He first served Tang Zhuangzong as a junior officer and had merit in campaigns.

units.zh: 唐天成中，自捧聖指揮使領澄州刺史，遷左右羽林都校。
units.en: During the Tiancheng reign he rose from commander of the Pengsheng Guard to prefect of Cheng Prefecture, then became chief of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Tang he went from commander of the Pengsheng Guard to prefect of Cheng Prefecture, then was transferred to chief of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards.

units.zh: 從藥彥稠討楊彥溫於河中，平之。
units.en: He followed Yao Yanchou in the campaign against Yang Yanwen at Hezhong and helped suppress the rebellion.
units.literal: He followed Yao Yanchou to attack Yang Yanwen at Hezhong and pacified him.

units.zh: 長興中，領壽州忠正軍節度使，加檢校太保、侍衛步軍都指揮使。
units.en: During the Changxing reign he served as military governor of the Zhongzheng Army at Shou Prefecture and was given the additional titles of acting Grand Guardian and commander of the palace guard infantry.
units.literal: In the Changxing era he held the post of military governor of the Zhongzheng Army at Shou Prefecture and was given the additional titles of acting Grand Guardian and commander of the palace guard infantry.

units.zh: 從賓素便佞，每進言，明宗多納之。
units.en: Congbin was a skilled flatterer, and Mingzong often accepted his advice.
units.literal: Congbin was by nature skilled in flattery; whenever he offered advice Mingzong often accepted it.

units.zh: 有供奉官丁延徽者，性貪狡，時奉詔監廩，以犯贓下獄，權貴多為救解，明宗怒，不許。
units.en: A palace attendant named Ding Yanhui was greedy and cunning. While supervising the granaries on imperial orders he was imprisoned for corruption. Many powerful men pleaded for him, but Mingzong refused in anger.
units.literal: There was a palace attendant named Ding Yanhui, greedy and cunning by nature; at the time he was ordered to supervise the granaries and was imprisoned for corruption; many powerful men pleaded for him, but Mingzong was angry and would not allow it.

units.zh: 從賓因奏他事，言及延徽，明宗曰：「非但爾言，蘇秦說予，亦不得也。」
units.en: Congbin raised another matter and spoke up for Yanhui. Mingzong said, "Even if Su Qin himself pleaded for him, it would do no good."
units.literal: Congbin, while memorializing on another matter, spoke of Yanhui; Mingzong said, "Not only your words—even if Su Qin spoke to me, it would not avail."

units.zh: 延徽竟就戮。
units.en: Yanhui was executed in the end.
units.literal: Yanhui was finally executed.

units.zh: 長興末，從賓出鎮靈武，加檢校太傅。
units.en: Late in the Changxing reign Congbin was posted to Lingwu as military governor and given the additional title of acting Grand Tutor.
units.literal: At the end of Changxing Congbin went out to govern Lingwu and was given the additional title of acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 高祖即位，受代入覲，會駕東幸，留從賓警巡洛下。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Congbin was relieved and came to court for audience. When the emperor traveled east, Congbin was left to patrol Luoyang.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, he was relieved and entered court for audience; it happened that the imperial carriage went east, and Congbin was left to patrol and guard Luoyang.

units.zh: 一日，逢留司御史於天津橋，從兵百人，不分路而過，排御史於水中，從賓紿奏其酒醉，其兇傲如此。
units.en: One day he met the acting censor on Tianjin Bridge. With a hundred followers he refused to yield the road and pushed the censor into the water. Congbin falsely reported that the man was drunk. That was how brutal and arrogant he was.
units.literal: One day he met the acting censor on Tianjin Bridge; with a hundred followers he would not yield the road and pushed the censor into the water; Congbin falsely reported that the man was drunk—such was his arrogance and violence.

units.zh: 及範延光據鄴城叛，詔從賓為副部署使，從楊光遠同討延光。
units.en: When Fan Yanguang rebelled and held Ye, Congbin was ordered to serve as deputy overall commander under Yang Guangyuan in the campaign against him.
units.literal: When Fan Yanguang held Ye city and rebelled, Congbin was ordered to be deputy overall commander and follow Yang Guangyuan in attacking Yanguang.

units.zh: 會延光使人誘從賓，從賓時在河陽，乃起兵以應之。
units.en: Yanguang sent envoys to entice him. Congbin was then at Heyang and raised troops in response.
units.literal: It happened that Yanguang sent men to entice Congbin; Congbin was then at Heyang and therefore raised troops in response.

units.zh: 先害皇子重信，及入洛，又害皇子重乂，取內庫金帛以給部伍，因東據汜水關，且欲觀望軍勢。
units.en: He first killed Prince Chongxin. After entering Luoyang he also killed Prince Chongyi, seized gold and silk from the inner treasury to pay his troops, seized Sishui Pass to the east, and waited to see how the armies fared.
units.literal: He first killed the prince Chongxin; when he entered Luoyang he also killed the prince Chongyi, took gold and silk from the inner treasury to pay his troops, and then held Sishui Pass in the east while wishing to watch how the armies fared.

units.zh: 高祖命杜重威、侯益分兵討之，從賓大敗，乘馬入河，溺水而死焉。
units.en: Gaozu ordered Du Chongwei and Hou Yi to attack him with divided forces. Congbin was routed, rode his horse into the river, and drowned.
units.literal: The High Ancestor ordered Du Chongwei and Hou Yi to divide their forces and attack him; Congbin was greatly defeated, rode his horse into the river, and drowned.

units.zh: 張延播者，汶陽人也。
units.en: Zhang Yanbo came from Wenyang.
units.literal: Zhang Yanbo was a native of Wenyang.

units.zh: 始為郡之牙將，唐同光初，明宗下其城，因收隸左右。
units.en: He first served as a guard officer of the commandery. Early in the Tongguang reign, when Mingzong captured his city, he was brought into Mingzong's personal retinue.
units.literal: At first he was a guard officer of the commandery; at the beginning of the Tongguang era of Tang, when Mingzong took his city, he was received into the personal retinue.

units.zh: 天成中，累授檢校司空、兩河發運營田使、柳州刺史。
units.en: During the Tiancheng reign he was successively appointed Honorary Minister of Works, commissioner for transport and agricultural garrison of the Two Rivers, and prefect of Liuzhou.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was successively appointed Honorary Minister of Works, commissioner for transport and agricultural garrison of the Two Rivers, and prefect of Liuzhou.

units.zh: 長興元年，出牧蔡州，加檢校司徒，入為左領軍衛大將軍，充客省使。
units.en: In Changxing 1 he was sent out to govern Caizhou, promoted to acting Grand Mentor, appointed grand general of the Left Imperial Guards Army, and made commissioner of the guest bureau.
units.literal: In the first year of Changxing he went out to govern Caizhou, was given the additional title of acting Grand Mentor, entered office as grand general of the Left Imperial Guards Army, and served as commissioner of the guest bureau.

units.zh: 伐蜀之役，命為馬軍都監。
units.en: During the campaign against Shu he was made cavalry inspector.
units.literal: In the campaign against Shu he was ordered to be cavalry inspector.

units.zh: 三年，遷鳳州防禦使、西面水陸轉運使。
units.en: In the third year he became defense commissioner of Fengzhou and Western land-and-water transport commissioner.
units.literal: In the third year he was transferred to defense commissioner of Fengzhou and Western land-and-water transport commissioner.

units.zh: 高祖即位，除東都副留守。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed deputy defender of the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor ascended the throne, he was made deputy defender of the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 車駕幸汴，遣兼洛京巡檢使。
units.en: When the emperor visited Bian, he was also appointed capital patrol commissioner for Luoyang.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Bian, he was sent also to serve as capital patrol commissioner for Luoyang.

units.zh: 張從賓作亂，令延播知河南府事。
units.en: When Zhang Congbin rebelled, Yanbo was put in charge of Henan Prefecture.
units.literal: When Zhang Congbin rebelled, Yanbo was ordered to administer Henan Prefecture.

units.zh: 從賓敗，伏誅。
units.en: When Congbin was defeated, Yanbo was executed.
units.literal: When Congbin was defeated, Yanbo was executed.

units.zh: 楊光遠，小字阿檀，及長，止名檀，唐天成中，以明宗改御名為亶，以偏傍字犯之，始改名光遠，字德明，其先沙陀部人也。
units.en: Yang Guangyuan's childhood name was Atan; as an adult he used only Tan. During the Tiancheng reign, when Mingzong changed his imperial name to Dan, Tan shared a radical component and was taboo, so he took the name Guangyuan, courtesy name Deming. His ancestors were Shatuo.
units.literal: Yang Guangyuan, childhood name Atan; when grown he used only the name Tan; in the Tiancheng era of Tang, because Mingzong changed his imperial name to Dan and the character shared a radical component, he first changed his name to Guangyuan, courtesy name Deming; his ancestors were of the Shatuo tribe.

units.zh: 父阿噔啜，後改名瑊，事唐武皇為隊長。
units.en: His father Adengchuo later changed his name to Jian and served Emperor Wu of Tang (Tang Wuhuang) as a company commander.
units.literal: His father Adengchuo later changed his name to Jian and served Tang Emperor Wu (Wuhuang) as a company commander.

units.zh: 光遠事莊宗為騎將，唐天祐中，莊宗遣振武節度使周德威討劉守光於幽州，因令光遠隸於德威麾下。
units.en: Guangyuan served Zhuangzong as a cavalry commander. In the Tianyou era Zhuangzong sent Zhende Army military governor Zhou Dewei against Liu Shouguang at Youzhou and placed Guangyuan under his command.
units.literal: Guangyuan served Zhuangzong as a cavalry commander; in the Tianyou era of Tang, Zhuangzong sent Zhende Army military governor Zhou Dewei to attack Liu Shouguang at Youzhou and had Guangyuan placed under Dewei's command.

units.zh: 後與德威拒契丹於新州，一軍以深入致敗，因傷其臂，遂廢，罷於家。
units.en: Later he and Dewei fought the Khitan at Xin Prefecture. The army was defeated after advancing too deep, Guangyuan's arm was wounded, and he was invalided out of service and sent home.
units.literal: Later he and Dewei resisted the Khitan at Xin Prefecture; the whole army was defeated because it had advanced too deep, and his arm was wounded; he was therefore disabled and dismissed to his home.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，思其戰功，命為幽州馬步軍都指揮使、檢校尚書右僕射，戍瓦橋關久之。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne he remembered Guangyuan's service and appointed him commander of the Youzhou horse and foot armies and acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, with a long posting at Waqiao Pass.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he recalled his battle merit and appointed him commander of the Youzhou horse and foot armies and acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, garrisoning Waqiao Pass for a long time.

units.zh: 明宗朝，歷媯、瀛、易、冀四州刺史。
units.en: Under Mingzong he served in turn as prefect of Gui, Ying, Yi, and Ji prefectures.
units.literal: In Mingzong's reign he successively held the four prefectures of Gui, Ying, Yi, and Ji.

units.zh: 光遠雖不識字，然有口辯，通於吏理，在郡有政聲，明宗頗重之。
units.en: Although Guangyuan could not read, he was eloquent and understood administration. His prefectures earned him a reputation for good government, and Mingzong valued him highly.
units.literal: Although Guangyuan could not read characters, he had eloquence in speech and was versed in administrative principle; in the prefectures he had a reputation for good government, and Mingzong valued him highly.

units.zh: 長興中，契丹有中山之敗，生擒其將紮拉等數十人，送於闕下，其後契丹既通和，遣使乞歸之，明宗與大臣謀議，特放還蕃。
units.en: During the Changxing reign the Khitan suffered a defeat at Zhongshan and dozens of their commanders including Zhala were captured and sent to court. After peace was made the Khitan asked for their return. Mingzong consulted his ministers and was inclined to release them.
units.literal: In the Changxing era the Khitan suffered defeat at Zhongshan; several dozen of their generals including Zhala were captured alive and sent to the court; later, when the Khitan had made peace, they sent envoys asking for their return; Mingzong deliberated with his ministers and specially ordered them sent back to the barbarians.

units.zh: 一日，召光遠於便殿言其事，光遠曰：「紮拉等北土之善戰者，彼失之如喪手足；
units.en: One day Mingzong summoned Guangyuan to the informal hall to discuss the matter. Guangyuan said, "Zhala and the others are the Khitan's best fighters in the north. Losing them is like losing hands and feet.
units.literal: One day he summoned Guangyuan to the informal hall to speak of the matter; Guangyuan said, "Zhala and the others are the Khitan's best fighters in the north; for them to lose these men is like losing hands and feet;

units.zh: 又在此累年，備諳中國事，若放還非便。」
units.en: They have been here for years and know China well. Sending them back would be unwise."
units.literal: moreover they have been here many years and are fully versed in affairs of China—if they are sent back it will not be advantageous."

units.zh: 明宗曰：「蕃人重盟誓，既通歡好，必不相負。」
units.en: Mingzong said, "The Khitan value sworn alliances. Now that we are at peace, they will not betray us."
units.literal: Mingzong said, "The barbarians value sworn alliances; now that we have friendly relations, they will surely not fail us."

units.zh: 光遠曰：「臣恐後悔不及也。」
units.en: Guangyuan said, "I fear you will regret it when it is too late."
units.literal: Guangyuan said, "Your servant fears you will regret it too late."

units.zh: 明宗遂止，深嘉其抗直。
units.en: Mingzong halted the plan and deeply praised his blunt honesty.
units.literal: Mingzong thereupon stopped and deeply praised his forthright resistance.

units.zh: 後自振武節度使移鎮中山，累加檢校太傅，將兵戍蔚州。
units.en: Later he moved from the Zhende Army to Zhongshan, was repeatedly promoted to acting Grand Tutor, and led troops garrisoning Yu Prefecture.
units.literal: Later he moved from military governor of the Zhende Army to govern Zhongshan, was repeatedly given the additional title of acting Grand Tutor, and led troops to garrison Yu Prefecture.

units.zh: 高祖舉義於太原，唐末帝遣光遠與張敬達屯兵於城下，俄而契丹大至，為其所敗，圍其寨久之，軍中糧絕，光遠乃與次將安審琦等殺敬達，擁眾歸命。
units.en: When Gaozu raised his banner at Taiyuan, the last Tang emperor sent Guangyuan and Zhang Jingda to besiege the city. The Khitan soon arrived in force, defeated them, and besieged their camp for a long time until provisions ran out. Guangyuan then joined his second-in-command An Shenqi and others in killing Jingda and leading the army to submit.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor raised the righteous cause at Taiyuan, the last Tang emperor sent Guangyuan and Zhang Jingda to encamp their troops below the city; before long the Khitan arrived in force, defeated them, and besieged their camp for a long time; provisions in the army were exhausted; Guangyuan then with the second commander An Shenqi and others killed Jingda and led the host to submit.

units.zh: 從高祖入洛，加檢校太尉，充宣武軍節度使、同平章事，判六軍諸衛事。
units.en: He followed Gaozu into Luoyang and was made acting Grand Commandant, military governor of the Xuanwu Army, Associate Grand Councillor, and overseer of the Six Armies and palace guards.
units.literal: Following the High Ancestor into Luoyang, he was given the additional title of acting Grand Commandant, made military governor of the Xuanwu Army and Associate Grand Councillor, and assigned to oversee the Six Armies and the palace guards.

units.zh: 是時，光遠每對高祖，常悒然不樂，高祖慮有不足，密遣近臣訊之。
units.en: At that time Guangyuan often seemed gloomy and unhappy in Gaozu's presence. Gaozu feared something was wrong and secretly sent a close minister to inquire.
units.literal: At that time, whenever Guangyuan faced the High Ancestor he was often gloomy and unhappy; the High Ancestor feared something was lacking and secretly sent a close minister to inquire.

units.zh: 光遠附奏曰：「臣貴為將相，非有不足，但以張生鐵死得其所，臣弗如也，衷心內愧，是以不樂。」
units.en: Guangyuan added to his memorial: "I hold the exalted rank of general and minister and lack for nothing. Yet Zhang Sheng Tie died where he ought — I am not his equal. That shame sits in my heart, and that is why I am unhappy."
units.literal: Guangyuan added in his memorial, saying, "Your subject holds the exalted rank of general and minister — there is nothing lacking — but Zhang Sheng Tie died in his proper place; I am not his equal. In my inmost heart I feel shame within, and therefore I am not joyful."

units.zh: 生鐵，蓋敬達之小字也。
units.en: Sheng Tie was the childhood name of Zhang Jingda.
units.literal: Sheng Tie was Jingda's childhood name.

units.zh: 高祖聞其言，以光遠為忠純之最者也。
units.en: When Gaozu heard this, he took Guangyuan to be the very model of loyalty and sincerity.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor heard these words, he considered Guangyuan the most loyal and pure of men.

units.zh: 其實光遠故為其言，以邀高祖之重信也。
units.en: In truth Guangyuan had spoken this way deliberately, to win Gaozu's deep trust.
units.literal: In truth Guangyuan deliberately spoke thus in order to win the High Ancestor's deep trust.

units.zh: 明年，範延光據鄴城叛，高祖命光遠率師討之。
units.en: The next year Fan Yanguang seized Ye and rebelled. Gaozu ordered Guangyuan to lead an army against him.
units.literal: The next year Fan Yanguang seized Ye city and rebelled; the High Ancestor ordered Guangyuan to lead troops to attack him.

units.zh: 將濟河，會滑州軍亂，時軍眾欲推光遠為主。
units.en: As he was about to cross the river, the army at Huazhou mutinied, and the troops wanted to make Guangyuan their leader.
units.literal: When he was about to cross the river, a mutiny broke out in the army at Huazhou; at the time the troops wished to make Guangyuan their leader.

units.zh: 光遠曰：「自古有折臂天子乎？
units.en: Guangyuan said, "Since antiquity, has there ever been an emperor with a broken arm?
units.literal: Guangyuan said, "Since antiquity has there ever been an emperor with a broken arm?

units.zh: 且天子豈公輩販弄之物？
units.en: And is the Son of Heaven something for the likes of you to barter and play with?
units.literal: Moreover, is the Son of Heaven a thing for you fellows to trade and manipulate?

units.zh: 晉陽之降，乃勢所窮迫，今若為之，直反賊也。」
units.en: The surrender at Jinyang came only because circumstances left no choice. If you do this now, you are simply turning rebel."
units.literal: The surrender at Jinyang was because circumstances had forced one to the limit; if you do this now, it is simply to turn rebel."

units.zh: 由是其下惕然，無復言者。
units.en: At that his men grew fearful, and no one spoke of it again.
units.literal: At this his subordinates became fearful, and there were no more who spoke of it.

units.zh: 高祖聞之，尤加寵重。
units.en: When Gaozu heard of it, he favored Guangyuan all the more.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor heard of it, he showed him even greater favor and esteem.

units.zh: 光遠既圍延光，尋授魏博行府節度使。
units.en: After Guangyuan besieged Yanguang, he was soon made acting military commissioner of Weibo.
units.literal: Once Guangyuan had besieged Yanguang, he was soon appointed acting military commissioner of Weibo.

units.zh: 兵柄在手，以為高祖懼己，稍干預朝政，或抗有所奏，高祖亦曲從之。
units.en: With military power in his hands, he believed Gaozu feared him. He began to meddle in court affairs, and when he submitted bold petitions, Gaozu yielded to him.
units.literal: With military authority in hand, he believed the High Ancestor feared him; he gradually intervened in court politics, and when he boldly submitted petitions, the High Ancestor also yielded to him.

units.zh: 復下詔以其子承祚尚長安公主，次子承信皆授美官。
units.en: Another edict appointed his son Chengzuo to marry Princess Chang'an and gave his second son Chengxin prestigious offices.
units.literal: An edict was again issued appointing his son Chengzuo to marry Princess Chang'an, and his second son Chengxin was granted fine offices.

units.zh: 恩渥殊等，為當時之冠。
units.en: The favor shown him was unmatched, the greatest of his day.
units.literal: Favor and bounty of special rank — foremost of his time.

units.zh: 桑維翰為樞密使，往往彈射其事，光遠心銜之。
units.en: Sang Weihan, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, often attacked him on these matters, and Guangyuan nursed a grievance.
units.literal: Sang Weihan served as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and often impeached him on these matters; Guangyuan bore a grudge in his heart.

units.zh: 及延光降，光遠入朝，面奏維翰擅權。
units.en: After Yanguang surrendered, Guangyuan came to court and accused Weihan face to face of monopolizing power.
units.literal: When Yanguang surrendered, Guangyuan entered court and in person memorialized that Weihan monopolized power.

units.zh: 高祖以光遠方有功於國，乃出維翰鎮相州，光遠為西京留守，兼鎮河陽，因罷其兵權。
units.en: Because Guangyuan had just rendered great service, Gaozu sent Weihan out to govern Xiangzhou, made Guangyuan defender of the Western Capital with concurrent command of Heyang, and thereby stripped him of military authority.
units.literal: The High Ancestor, because Guangyuan had just rendered great service to the state, sent Weihan out to govern Xiangzhou, made Guangyuan defender of the Western Capital while also governing Heyang, and thereby removed his military authority.

units.zh: 光遠由此怨望，潛貯異志，多以珍玩奉契丹，訴己之屈，又私養部曲千餘人，撓法犯禁，河、洛之人，恒如備盜。
units.en: From this Guangyuan turned resentful and secretly harbored other ambitions. He often sent rare treasures to the Khitan while complaining of his mistreatment, and privately kept more than a thousand retainers who broke the law with impunity. The people of the Yellow River valley and Luoyang lived as though on guard against robbers.
units.literal: From this Guangyuan nursed resentment, secretly harbored divergent ambitions, often sent rare treasures to the Khitan as tribute while lamenting his own grievance, and privately maintained more than a thousand retainers, disturbing the law and violating prohibitions — the people of the Yellow River region and Luoyang lived as though guarding against bandits.

units.zh: 尋冊拜太尉、兼中書令。
units.en: Soon he was appointed Grand Marshal and concurrently Director of the Chancellery.
units.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Grand Marshal and concurrently appointed Director of the Chancellery.

units.zh: 時範延光致仕，輦囊裝妓妾，居於河陽。
units.en: At that time Fan Yanguang had retired from office. He moved to Heyang with cartloads of concubines and entertainers.
units.literal: At that time Fan Yanguang had retired from office, transporting chests filled with concubines and entertainers, and residing at Heyang.

units.zh: 光遠利其奇貨，且慮為子孫之讎，因奏延光不家汴、洛，出舍外藩，非南走淮夷，則北走契丹，宜早除之。
units.en: Guangyuan coveted Yanguang's extraordinary wealth and also feared vengeance for his descendants. He memorialized that Yanguang did not live in Bian or Luoyang but had taken up residence outside the capital, and would either flee south to the Huai tribes or north to the Khitan — he should be eliminated at once.
units.literal: Guangyuan coveted his extraordinary goods and also feared vengeance for his descendants; he therefore memorialized that Yanguang did not dwell in Bian or Luoyang but lived outside the frontier, and would either flee south to the Huai tribes or north to the Khitan — he should be removed early.

units.zh: 高祖以許之不死，鐵券在焉，持疑未允。
units.en: Gaozu had promised that Yanguang would not be killed, and the iron certificate of mercy still stood, so he hesitated and would not agree.
units.literal: The High Ancestor, because he had promised that Yanguang would not die and the iron certificate still stood, hesitated and did not approve.

units.zh: 光遠乃遣子承勛以甲士圍其第，逼令自裁。
units.en: Guangyuan then sent his son Chengxun with armored troops to surround Yanguang's residence and forced him to kill himself.
units.literal: Guangyuan then sent his son Chengxun with armored soldiers to surround his residence and forced him to take his own life.

units.zh: 延光曰：「天子在上，安得如此！」
units.en: Yanguang said, "The Son of Heaven is above — how can you do this!"
units.literal: Yanguang said, "The Son of Heaven is above — how can this be done!"

units.zh: 乃遣使者乞移居洛下，行及河橋，擯於流而溺殺之，矯奏雲延光自投河，朝廷以適會其意，弗之理。
units.en: He then sent envoys asking to move to Luoyang. When he reached the river bridge, they pushed him into the current and drowned him, then falsely reported that Yanguang had thrown himself into the river. The court, as this suited their purpose, did not pursue the matter.
units.literal: He then sent envoys begging to move and live below Luoyang; when he reached the river bridge, they pushed him into the current and drowned him, falsely reporting that Yanguang had thrown himself into the river — the court, as this happened to suit their intent, did not pursue the matter.

units.zh: 後逾歲入覲，高祖為置曲宴，教坊伶人以光遠暴斂重賦，因陳戲譏之，光遠殊無慚色。
units.en: More than a year later he came to court for an audience. Gaozu held a banquet with music, and musicians from the Directorate of Education performed a skit mocking Guangyuan for his ruthless levies and heavy taxes. Guangyuan showed not the least shame.
units.literal: More than a year later he entered court for an audience; the High Ancestor held a banquet with music, and musicians from the Directorate of Education, because Guangyuan had ruthlessly levied heavy taxes, performed a skit mocking him — Guangyuan showed not the least shame.

units.zh: 高祖謂光遠曰：「元城之役，卿左右皆立功，未曾旌賞，今各與一郡，俾厘任以榮之。」
units.en: Gaozu said to Guangyuan, "At Yuancheng, all those at your side rendered service yet were never rewarded. Now each shall receive a commandery, that they may take up office and be honored."
units.literal: The High Ancestor said to Guangyuan, "In the campaign at Yuancheng, all those at your side rendered merit yet were never honored with rewards; now each shall receive one commandery, that they may carry out duties and be glorified."

units.zh: 因命為刺史者凡數人。
units.en: Several men were then appointed prefects.
units.literal: Several men were thus appointed prefects.

units.zh: 時王建立自青州移鎮上黨，乃以光遠為平盧軍節度使，封東平王。
units.en: When Wang Jianli was transferred from Qingzhou to govern Shangdang, Guangyuan was made military commissioner of the Pinglu Army and enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.
units.literal: At that time Wang Jianli moved from Qingzhou to govern Shangdang; Guangyuan was made military commissioner of the Pinglu Army and enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.

units.zh: 光遠面奏，請與長子同行，尋授承勛萊州防禦使。
units.en: Guangyuan memorialized in person asking that his eldest son accompany him, and Chengxun was soon appointed defender of Laizhou.
units.literal: Guangyuan memorialized in person requesting that his eldest son accompany him; Chengxun was soon appointed defender of Laizhou.

units.zh: 及赴任，仆從妓妾至千餘騎，滿盈僭侈，為方嶽之最。
units.en: When he went to take up his post, attendants and entertainers numbered more than a thousand riders — extravagance beyond all proper bounds, the most excessive of any regional governor.
units.literal: When he went to take up his post, attendants and entertainers numbered more than a thousand riders — overflowing extravagance beyond proper rank, the most extreme among regional governors.

units.zh: 下車之後，惟以刻剝為事。
units.en: After taking office he devoted himself solely to extortion.
units.literal: After taking office he devoted himself solely to extortion.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，冊拜太師，封壽王。
units.en: When Shaodi succeeded to the throne, Guangyuan was appointed Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.
units.literal: When Shaodi succeeded to the throne, Guangyuan was enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and Prince of Shou.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·馬仁鎬傳》：晉天福中，青州楊光遠將圖不軌，以仁鎬為節度副使，伺其動靜。
units.en: ("History of Song," Biography of Ma Rengao: During the Jin Tianfu era, Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou was plotting rebellion. He appointed Rengao deputy military commissioner to watch his movements.
units.literal: ("History of Song," Biography of Ma Rengao: In the Tianfu era of Jin, Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou was plotting rebellion; he appointed Rengao as deputy military commissioner to observe his movements.

units.zh: 歷二年，或譖仁鎬於朝，改護國軍行軍司馬。
units.en: After two years someone slandered Rengao at court, and he was transferred to military adjutant of the Huguo Army on expedition.
units.literal: After two years, someone slandered Rengao at court; he was transferred to military adjutant of the Huguo Army on expedition.

units.zh: 仁鎬至河中數月，光遠反書聞。）〉
units.en: A few months after Rengao reached Hezhong, news of Guangyuan's rebellion arrived.)〉
units.literal: When Rengao reached Hezhong after several months, news of Guangyuan's rebellion arrived.)〉

units.zh: 後因景延廣上言，請取光遠麾下所借官馬二百匹，光遠怒曰：「此馬先帝賜我，何以復取？
units.en: Later Jing Yanguang memorialized asking that two hundred government horses borrowed by Guangyuan's forces be reclaimed. Guangyuan angrily said, "These horses were granted me by the late emperor — why take them back?
units.literal: Later, because Jing Yanguang memorialized requesting two hundred government horses borrowed by Guangyuan's forces, Guangyuan angrily said, "These horses were granted me by the late emperor — why take them back?

units.zh: 是疑我也。」
units.en: This means you distrust me."
units.literal: This means you distrust me."

units.zh: 遂遣人潛召取子承祚自單州奔歸，朝廷乃就除淄州刺史，以從其便。
units.en: He then secretly sent men to summon his son Chengzuo back from Shanzhou. The court thereupon appointed Chengzuo prefect of Zibo to accommodate him.
units.literal: He then secretly sent men to summon his son Chengzuo back from Shanzhou; the court thereupon appointed him prefect of Zibo to accommodate his convenience.

units.zh: 光遠益驕，因此構契丹，述少帝違好之短，且言大饑之後，國用空虛，此時一舉可以平定。
units.en: Guangyuan grew ever more arrogant. He then conspired with the Khitan, recounting Shaodi's breaches of the alliance and saying that after the great famine the treasury was empty — one stroke at this moment could settle everything.
units.literal: Guangyuan grew ever more arrogant; he therefore conspired with the Khitan, recounting Shaodi's breaches of their alliance and saying that after the great famine the state treasury was empty — at this moment one blow could settle everything.

units.zh: 開運元年正月，契丹南牧，陷我博陵，少帝幸澶淵。
units.en: In the first month of the first year of Kaiyun the Khitan drove south, captured Boling, and Shaodi went to Chanyuan.
units.literal: In the first month of the first year of Kaiyun the Khitan drove their herds south, captured our Boling, and Shaodi proceeded to Chanyuan.

units.zh: 三月，契丹退，命李守貞、符彥卿率師東討。
units.en: In the third month the Khitan withdrew. Shaodi ordered Li Shouzhen and Fu Yanqing to lead an army east against Guangyuan.
units.literal: In the third month the Khitan withdrew; Shaodi ordered Li Shouzhen and Fu Yanqing to lead troops east to attack.

units.zh: 光遠素無兵眾，惟嬰城自守，守貞以長連城圍之。
units.en: Guangyuan had never commanded many troops and could only hold the city and defend himself. Shouzhen surrounded it with a long linked wall of siege works.
units.literal: Guangyuan had never had many troops; he could only hold the city and defend himself. Shouzhen surrounded it with a long linked wall.

units.zh: 冬十一月，承勛與弟承信、承祚見城中人民相食將盡，知事不濟，勸光遠乞降，冀免於赤族。
units.en: In the eleventh month of winter Chengxun and his brothers Chengxin and Chengzuo saw the people in the city eating one another and nearly exhausted. Knowing the cause was lost, they urged Guangyuan to surrender, hoping to spare the whole clan from extermination.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of winter Chengxun, together with his brothers Chengxin and Chengzuo, saw the people in the city eating one another and nearly exhausted; knowing the affair would not succeed, they urged Guangyuan to beg surrender, hoping to escape extermination of the whole clan.

units.zh: 光遠不納，曰：「我在代北時，嘗以紙錢駝馬祭天池，皆沈沒，人言合有天子分，宜且待時，勿輕言降也。」
units.en: Guangyuan refused. He said, "When I was in northern Dai, I once sacrificed paper money, camels, and horses at the Heavenly Pool, and all sank beneath the water. People said I was destined for a Son of Heaven's portion. We should wait for the right moment and not speak lightly of surrender."
units.literal: Guangyuan would not accept this and said, "When I was in northern Dai, I once offered paper money, camels, and horses in sacrifice at the Heavenly Pool, and all sank beneath the water. People said I was destined to have a Son of Heaven's portion; we should wait for the time and not lightly speak of surrender."

units.zh: 承勛慮禍在朝夕，與諸弟同謀，殺節度判官邱濤，親校杜延壽、楊瞻、白延祚等，梟其首，乃遣承祚送於守貞。
units.en: Chengxun, fearing disaster within days, plotted with his brothers. They killed the military commissioner-assistant Qiu Tao and the personal officers Du Yanshou, Yang Zhan, Bai Yanzuo, and others, displayed their heads, and sent Chengzuo to deliver them to Shouzhen.
units.literal: Chengxun, fearing disaster was at hand within days, plotted together with his brothers, killed the military commissioner-assistant Qiu Tao and the personal officers Du Yanshou, Yang Zhan, Bai Yanzuo, and others, displayed their heads, and then sent Chengzuo to deliver them to Shouzhen.

units.zh: 因縱火大噪，劫其父幽於私第，以城納款，遣即墨縣令王德柔貢表待罪，光遠亦上章自首。
units.en: They then set fires and raised a great clamor, seized their father and confined him in a private residence, and surrendered the city. They sent Jimo county magistrate Wang Derou with a memorial accepting guilt, and Guangyuan also submitted a confession.
units.literal: They then set fires and raised a great clamor, seized their father and confined him in a private residence, surrendered the city, sent Jimo county magistrate Wang Derou to present a memorial accepting guilt, and Guangyuan also submitted a memorial confessing his crime.

units.zh: 少帝以頃歲太原歸命，欲曲全之，執政曰：「豈有逆狀滔天而赦之也？」
units.en: Shaodi, mindful that Taiyuan had submitted only a few years before, wished to spare Guangyuan if possible. The chief ministers said, "How can treason reaching to heaven be pardoned?"
units.literal: Shaodi, because Taiyuan had submitted in recent years, wished to spare him as far as possible; the chief ministers said, "How can there be treason reaching to heaven yet still grant pardon?"

units.zh: 乃命守貞便宜處置。
units.en: He therefore ordered Shouzhen to dispose of the matter as he saw fit.
units.literal: He therefore ordered Shouzhen to dispose of the matter as circumstances required.

units.zh: 守貞遣人拉殺之，
units.en: Shouzhen sent men to strangle him to death,
units.literal: Shouzhen sent men to strangle him to death,

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：守貞遣客省副使何延祚殺之於其家。
units.en: ("History of the Five Dynasties": Shouzhen sent He Yanzuo, deputy commissioner of the Reception Bureau, to kill him in his home.
units.literal: ("History of the Five Dynasties": Shouzhen sent He Yanzuo, deputy commissioner of the Reception Bureau, to kill him in his home.

units.zh: 以病卒聞。）〉
units.en: His death was announced as illness.)〉
units.literal: It was announced that he had died of illness.)〉

units.zh: 漢高祖即位，詔贈尚書令，追封齊王，仍令立碑。
units.en: When Gaozu of Han ascended the throne, he posthumously granted Guangyuan the title of Director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed him posthumously as Prince of Qi, and ordered a stele erected.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Han ascended the throne, an edict posthumously granted him Director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed him posthumously as Prince of Qi, and ordered a stele erected.

units.zh: 未幾，其碑石無故自折，可知其陰責也。
units.en: Before long the stele stone broke in two for no apparent reason — a sign of the hidden reproach upon him.
units.literal: Before long the stele stone broke in two for no apparent reason — one may know the hidden reproach upon him.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：楊光遠滅範延光之後，朝廷以其功高，授青州節度，封東平王，奄有登、萊、沂、密數郡。
units.en: ("Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties": After Yang Guangyuan destroyed Fan Yanguang, the court, honoring his great merit, made him military commissioner of Qingzhou and Prince of Dongping, and he held Deng, Lai, Yi, Mi, and several other commanderies.
units.literal: ("Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties": After Yang Guangyuan destroyed Fan Yanguang, the court, because his merit was great, appointed him military commissioner of Qingzhou, enfeoffed him as Prince of Dongping, and he held several commanderies including Deng, Lai, Yi, and Mi.

units.zh: 既而自負強盛，舉兵反，朝廷以宋州節度李守貞嘗與光遠有隙，乃命李討之。
units.en: Then, confident in his strength, he rebelled. Because Li Shouzhen, military commissioner of Songzhou, had once been at odds with Guangyuan, the court ordered Li to attack him.
units.literal: Then, confident in his strength, he raised troops and rebelled; the court, because Li Shouzhen, military commissioner of Songzhou, had once had a rift with Guangyuan, ordered Li to attack him.

units.zh: 李受詔欣然，志在必取，莫不身先矢石。
units.en: Li received the order gladly, resolved to take Guangyuan, and always placed himself ahead amid arrows and stones.
units.literal: Li received the order gladly, resolved to take him, and none failed to place himself ahead amid arrows and stones.

units.zh: 光遠見而懼之，度不能禦，遂降。
units.en: Guangyuan saw this and was afraid. Judging that he could not hold out, he surrendered.
units.literal: Guangyuan saw this and feared him; judging that he could not resist, he surrendered.

units.zh: 初，光遠反書至，中外大震，時百官起居次，忽有朝士揚言於眾曰：「楊光遠欲謀大事，吾不信也。
units.en: When Guangyuan's letter of rebellion first arrived, court and country were greatly shaken. During the daily audience of the hundred officials, a court gentleman suddenly declared aloud, "Yang Guangyuan is plotting a great rebellion — I do not believe it.
units.literal: At first, when Guangyuan's letter of rebellion arrived, court and country were greatly shaken. At the time the hundred officials were assembled for the daily audience when suddenly a court gentleman declared aloud to the crowd, "Yang Guangyuan wishes to plot a great affair — I do not believe it.

units.zh: 光遠素患禿瘡，其妻又跛，自古豈有禿頭天子、跛腳皇后耶？」
units.en: Guangyuan has long suffered from bald sores, and his wife is lame — since antiquity, has there ever been a bald Son of Heaven or a lame empress?"
units.literal: Guangyuan has long suffered from bald sores, and his wife is also lame — since antiquity has there ever been a bald-headed Son of Heaven or a lame-footed empress?"

units.zh: 於是人心頓安，未幾，光遠果降。）〉
units.en: At that the people's hearts were instantly calmed. Before long Guangyuan did indeed surrender.)〉
units.literal: At this people's hearts were instantly calmed; before long Guangyuan indeed surrendered.)〉

units.zh: 承勛，光遠之長子也。
units.en: Chengxun was Guangyuan's eldest son.
units.literal: Chengxun was Guangyuan's eldest son.

units.zh: 始名承貴，避少帝名改焉。
units.en: His original name was Chenggui; he changed it to avoid the taboo on Shaodi's name.
units.literal: His original name was Chenggui; he changed it to avoid the taboo on Shaodi's name.

units.zh: 以父蔭歷光、濮州刺史，光遠兼鎮河陽，命制置三城事。
units.en: Through his father's privilege he served successively as prefect of Guang and Pu. When Guangyuan concurrently governed Heyang, Chengxun was ordered to manage affairs of the Three Cities.
units.literal: Through his father's privilege he successively served as prefect of Guang and Pu; when Guangyuan concurrently governed Heyang, he was ordered to manage affairs of the Three Cities.

units.zh: 光遠移鎮青州，授萊州防禦使。
units.en: When Guangyuan transferred to Qingzhou, Chengxun was appointed defender of Laizhou.
units.literal: When Guangyuan transferred to govern Qingzhou, Chengxun was appointed defender of Laizhou.

units.zh: 在郡亦頗理，嘗憤父側之奸黨，欲殺之，每省父，父為匿焉。
units.en: In the commandery he also governed fairly well. He once grew angry at the villainous faction surrounding his father and wished to kill them, but each time he visited his father, his father hid them away.
units.literal: In the commandery he also governed fairly well. He once grew angry at the villainous faction at his father's side and wished to kill them; each time he visited his father, his father hid them.

units.zh: 及光遠構釁，嬰城以叛，承勛赴之，敵退，為王師所圍。
units.en: When Guangyuan provoked conflict and held the city in rebellion, Chengxun went to join him. The enemy withdrew, and they were surrounded by the imperial army.
units.literal: When Guangyuan provoked conflict and held the city in rebellion, Chengxun went to join him; the enemy withdrew, and they were surrounded by the imperial army.

units.zh: 逾歲糧盡，與其弟承祚背父之命，出降王師，朝廷授汝州防禦使，尋改鄭州。
units.en: After more than a year the grain ran out. Together with his brother Chengzuo he defied his father's command, went out, and surrendered to the imperial army. The court appointed him defender of Ruzhou, then soon transferred him to Zhengzhou.
units.literal: After more than a year the grain was exhausted; together with his brother Chengzuo he defied his father's command, went out and surrendered to the imperial army, and the court appointed him defender of Ruzhou, soon changed to Zhengzhou.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·楊承信傳》：光遠死，承信與弟承祚詣闕請死。
units.en: ("History of Song," Biography of Yang Chengxin: When Guangyuan died, Chengxin and his brother Chengzuo went to court to beg for death.
units.literal: ("History of Song," Biography of Yang Chengxin: When Guangyuan died, Chengxin and his brother Chengzuo went to court to beg for death.

units.zh: 詔釋之，以承信為右羽林將軍，承祚為右驍衛將軍，放歸，服喪私第，尋安置鄭州。）〉
units.en: An edict released them. Chengxin was made general of the Right Feathered Forest and Chengzuo general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard. They were sent home to mourn in their private residence and were soon settled at Zhengzhou.)〉
units.literal: An edict released them; Chengxin was made general of the Right Feathered Forest and Chengzuo general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard. They were sent home to mourn in their private residence, and were soon settled at Zhengzhou.)〉

units.zh: 及契丹入汴，遣騎士自圃田召至，責其害父背己，使臠其肉而殺之。
units.en: When the Khitan entered Bian, they sent horsemen from Putian to summon him, rebuked him for killing his father and betraying them, had his flesh carved away piece by piece, and killed him.
units.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, they sent horsemen from Putian to summon him, rebuked him for killing his father and betraying them, had his flesh carved away, and killed him.

units.zh: 以其弟承信為青州節度使。
units.en: His brother Chengxin was made military commissioner of Qingzhou.
units.literal: His brother Chengxin was made military commissioner of Qingzhou.

units.zh: 盧文進，字國用，范陽人也。
units.en: Lu Wenjin, whose courtesy name was Guoyong, came from Fanyang.
units.literal: Lu Wenjin, courtesy name Guoyong, was a native of Fanyang.

units.zh: 身長七尺，飲啖過人，望之偉如也。
units.en: He stood seven feet tall, ate and drank more than other men, and looked imposing from afar.
units.literal: His body was seven feet tall; in eating and drinking he surpassed other men; seen from afar he looked imposing.

units.zh: 少事劉守光為騎將，唐莊宗攻燕，以文進首降，遙授壽州刺史。
units.en: In youth he served Liu Shouguang as a cavalry commander. When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong attacked Yan, Wenjin was the first to surrender and was appointed from afar as prefect of Shouzhou.
units.literal: In youth he served Liu Shouguang as a cavalry commander; when Tang Emperor Zhuangzong attacked Yan, Wenjin was the first to surrender and was appointed from afar as prefect of Shouzhou.

units.zh: 初，莊宗得山後八軍，以愛弟存矩為新州圍練使以總領之。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong first obtained the Eight Armies behind the mountains, he made his beloved younger brother Cunju regimental commissioner of Xinzhou to command them overall.
units.literal: At first, when Emperor Zhuangzong obtained the Eight Armies behind the mountains, he made his beloved younger brother Cunju regimental commissioner of Xinzhou to command them overall.

units.zh: 莊宗與劉鄩對壘於莘縣，命存矩於山後召募勁兵，又命山北居民出戰馬器仗，每鬻牛十頭易馬一匹，人心怨咨。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong faced Liu Yan in camp at Shen county. He ordered Cunju to recruit strong soldiers behind the mountains and also ordered the residents north of the mountains to supply war horses and weapons, exchanging one horse for every ten oxen sold. Resentment spread among the people.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong faced Liu Yan in camp at Shen county; he ordered Cunju to recruit strong soldiers behind the mountains and also ordered the residents north of the mountains to supply war horses and weapons; for every ten oxen sold one horse was exchanged — hearts were full of resentment and complaint.

units.zh: 時存矩團結五百騎，令文進將之，與存矩俱行。
units.en: At that time Cunju assembled five hundred cavalry and ordered Wenjin to lead them, and they traveled together.
units.literal: At that time Cunju assembled five hundred cavalry and ordered Wenjin to lead them, traveling together with Cunju.

units.zh: 至祁溝關，軍士聚謀曰：「我輩邊人，棄父母妻子，為他血戰，千里送死，固不能也。」
units.en: When they reached Qigou Pass the soldiers gathered to plot. They said, "We are frontier men who have abandoned parents, wives, and children to fight bloody battles for others. We cannot go a thousand li to deliver ourselves to death."
units.literal: When they reached Qigou Pass the soldiers gathered to plot, saying, "We are frontier men who have abandoned parents, wives, and children to fight bloody battles for others — to go a thousand li to deliver ourselves to death, we truly cannot."

units.zh: 眾曰：「擁盧將軍卻還新州，據城自守，奈我何！」
units.en: The crowd said, "Let us support General Lu, turn back to Xinzhou, hold the city, and defend ourselves — what can they do to us!"
units.literal: The crowd said, "Let us support General Lu and turn back to Xinzhou, hold the city and defend ourselves — what can they do to us!"

units.zh: 因大呼揮戈，趣傳舍，害存矩於榻下。
units.en: They then shouted and waved their spears, rushed to the relay station, and killed Cunju beneath his couch.
units.literal: They then shouted loudly and waved their spears, rushed to the relay station, and killed Cunju beneath his couch.

units.zh: 文進撫膺曰：「奴輩累我矣。」
units.en: Wenjin clutched his chest and said, "These wretched fellows have ruined me."
units.literal: Wenjin clutched his chest and said, "These slave fellows have ruined me."

units.zh: 因環屍而泣曰：「此輩既害郎君，我何面目見王！」
units.en: He then circled the corpse and wept. "Since these men have killed the young lord, with what face can I see the prince!"
units.literal: He then circled the corpse and wept, saying, "Since these fellows have killed the young lord, with what face can I see the prince!"

units.zh: 〈（案《遼史》：存矩取文進女為側室，文進心常內愧，因與亂軍殺存矩。）〉
units.en: (According to the "History of Liao": Cunju took Wenjin's daughter as a concubine. Wenjin always felt ashamed, and therefore joined the mutinous troops in killing Cunju.)〉
units.literal: (According to the "History of Liao": Cunju took Wenjin's daughter as a concubine; Wenjin always felt shame within his heart, and therefore joined the mutinous troops in killing Cunju.)〉

units.zh: 與薛史異因為亂軍所擁。
units.en: This differs from Xue Juzheng's History of the Five Dynasties: he was therefore carried off by the mutinous troops.
units.literal: This differs from the History of the Five Dynasties by Xue — he was therefore carried off by the mutinous troops.

units.zh: 反攻新州，不克；
units.en: He counterattacked Xinzhou but could not take it;
units.literal: He counterattacked Xinzhou but could not take it;

units.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書》：文進攻新州，不克，夜走墜塹，一躍而出，明日視之，乃郡之黑龍潭也，絕岸數丈，深不可測。
units.en: (Ma Ling's "Book of Southern Tang": Wenjin attacked Xinzhou but could not take it. Fleeing by night he fell into a ditch and leaped out in one bound. The next day he looked and saw it was the commandery's Black Dragon Pool, with sheer banks several zhang high and depths beyond measure.
units.literal: (Ma Ling's "Book of Southern Tang": Wenjin attacked Xinzhou but could not take it; fleeing by night he fell into a ditch, leaped out in one bound, and the next day looked and saw it was the commandery's Black Dragon Pool, with sheer banks several zhang high and depths beyond measure.

units.zh: 又嘗有大蛇，徑至座間，引首及膝，文進取食飼之而去。
units.en: On another occasion a great serpent came directly to his seat and raised its head to his knee. Wenjin took food, fed it, and it departed.
units.literal: On another occasion a great serpent came directly to his seat, raised its head to his knee; Wenjin took food, fed it, and it departed.

units.zh: 由是自負。）〉
units.en: From this he grew self-confident.)〉
units.literal: From this he grew self-confident.)〉

units.zh: 又攻武州，又不利。
units.en: He attacked Wuzhou again, again without success.
units.literal: He again attacked Wuzhou, and again met with no success.

units.zh: 周德威命將追討，文進遂奔契丹，命為幽州兵馬留後，部分漢軍，常別為營寨。
units.en: Zhou Dewei ordered generals to pursue him. Wenjin then fled to the Khitan, was appointed acting commander of troops and horses at Youzhou, was assigned Han troops, and usually encamped separately.
units.literal: Zhou Dewei ordered generals to pursue and attack; Wenjin then fled to the Khitan, was appointed acting commander of troops and horses at Youzhou, assigned Han troops, and usually encamped separately.

units.zh: 未幾，文進引契丹寇新州。
units.en: Before long Wenjin led the Khitan in a raid on Xinzhou.
units.literal: Before long Wenjin led the Khitan to raid Xinzhou.

units.zh: 自是北師數至，驅擄數州士女，教其織纴工作，中國所為者悉備，契丹所以強盛者，得文進之故也。
units.en: From then on northern armies came repeatedly, driving off and capturing men and women from several commanderies and teaching them weaving and other crafts. Everything done in China was fully provided. That the Khitan grew strong and flourishing was due to obtaining Wenjin.
units.literal: From this northern armies came repeatedly, driving off and capturing men and women of several commanderies, teaching them weaving and other work — everything done in China was fully provided; that the Khitan became strong and flourishing was due to obtaining Wenjin.

units.zh: 〈（案《遼史》云：文進引契丹軍攻新州，刺史安金全不能守，棄城去。
units.en: (According to the History of Liao: Wenjin led Khitan forces against Xin Prefecture. Prefect An Jinquan could not hold the city and fled.
units.literal: (According to the History of Liao: Wenjin led Khitan troops to attack Xin Prefecture; the prefect An Jinquan could not hold it and abandoned the city.

units.zh: 周德威援之，進攻新州，契丹眾數萬，德威不勝，大敗奔歸。
units.en: Zhou Dewei came to relieve the city and attacked Xin Prefecture. The Khitan numbered in the tens of thousands. Dewei was defeated and fled in rout.
units.literal: Zhou Dewei came to relieve him and advanced to attack Xin Prefecture; the Khitan numbered tens of thousands; Dewei could not prevail and was routed, fleeing back.

units.zh: 文進與契丹攻幽州，且二百日，城中圍困，晉王親將兵救之，方始解去。
units.en: Wenjin and the Khitan besieged Youzhou for nearly two hundred days. When the Prince of Jin led a relief army in person, they finally withdrew.
units.literal: Wenjin and the Khitan attacked Youzhou for nearly two hundred days; the city was besieged in distress; the Prince of Jin personally led troops to rescue it, and only then did they withdraw.

units.zh: 契丹以文進為幽州節度使，又以為盧龍節度使。）〉
units.en: The Khitan appointed him military governor of Youzhou and also of the Lulong Army.)〉
units.literal: The Khitan made Wenjin military governor of Youzhou and also military governor of the Lulong Army.)〉

units.zh: 同光之世，為患尤深。
units.en: During the Tongguang reign his depredations were especially severe.
units.literal: In the Tongguang era the harm he caused was especially deep.

units.zh: 文進在平州，率奚族勁騎，鳥擊獸搏，倏來忽往，燕、趙諸州，荊榛滿目。
units.en: From Ping Prefecture Wenjin led the Xi tribe's fierce cavalry in raids swift as birds and beasts. The prefectures of Yan and Zhao were left a wilderness of thorns.
units.literal: Wenjin was at Ping Prefecture, leading the Xi tribe's fierce cavalry; like birds striking and beasts fighting, they came suddenly and went suddenly; in the prefectures of Yan and Zhao, thorns and brambles filled the eye.

units.zh: 軍屯涿州，每歲運糧，自瓦橋至幽州，勁兵猛將，援遞糧車，然猶為契丹所鈔，奔命不暇，皆文進導之也。
units.en: Troops were stationed at Zhuo Prefecture. Each year grain was hauled from Waqiao to Youzhou under escort by crack troops and fierce generals, yet the Khitan still raided the convoys without cease—all at Wenjin's guidance.
units.literal: The army was encamped at Zhuo Prefecture; each year grain was transported from Waqiao to Youzhou; crack troops and fierce generals escorted the relay grain carts, yet still they were raided by the Khitan, rushing to their limits without rest—all guided by Wenjin.

units.zh: 及明宗即位之明年，文進自平州率所部十餘萬眾來奔。
units.en: The year after Mingzong took the throne, Wenjin defected from Ping Prefecture with more than a hundred thousand followers.
units.literal: In the year after Mingzong took the throne, Wenjin came to submit from Ping Prefecture at the head of more than a hundred thousand of his followers.

units.zh: 行及幽州，先遣使上表曰：「頃以新州團練使李存矩，提衡郡邑，掌握恩威，虐黎庶則毒甚於豺狼，聚賦斂則貪盈於溝壑，人不堪命，士各離心，臣即拋父母之邦，入朔漠之地。
units.en: Reaching Youzhou, he first sent a memorial: "Recently Li Cunju, regimental commissioner of Xin Prefecture, ruled the district with arbitrary power. He oppressed the people worse than wolves and hoarded taxes until his greed filled every ravine. The people could not endure it and the officers lost heart. I therefore abandoned my homeland and entered the northern steppe.
units.literal: When he reached Youzhou he first sent envoys with a memorial, saying, "Recently Li Cunju, regimental commissioner of Xin Prefecture, held the balance over commandery and district and grasped favor and awe; in oppressing the people his poison exceeded wolves; in gathering taxes and levies his greed filled gullies and ravines; the people could not bear their fate, officers each lost heart; your servant then cast aside the land of his parents and entered the northern desert.

units.zh: 幾年雁塞，徒向日以傾心；
units.en: For years on the frontier I turned my heart toward the sun in vain;
units.literal: For several years at the wild-goose frontier, in vain I turned my heart toward the sun;

units.zh: 一望家山，每銷魂而斷目。
units.en: and at every glimpse of home my soul broke and my sight failed.
units.literal: at one glimpse of home mountains, each time my soul dissolved and my sight broke.

units.zh: 李子卿之河畔，空有怨辭；
units.en: By the river of Li Ziqing I had only empty grievance;
units.literal: By the riverbank of Li Ziqing there were only empty words of grievance;

units.zh: 石季倫之樂中，莫陳歸引。
units.en: in the music of Shi Jilun I could voice no plea to return.
units.literal: in the music of Shi Jilun no plea for return could be voiced.

units.zh: 近聞皇帝陛下，皇天眷命，清明在躬，握紀乘乾，鼎新革故，始知大幸，有路朝宗，便貯歸心，祗伺良會。
units.en: I have lately heard that Your Majesty holds Heaven's mandate, governs with clarity, and has renewed the realm. I knew at last my great fortune and the road home. I stored my heart for return and reverently awaited the right moment.
units.literal: Recently I have heard that Your Majesty, Heaven's favored mandate upon you, clarity and brightness in your person, grasping the calendar and riding the celestial pivot, renewing the cauldron and reforming the old, I first knew great fortune and a road to pay court; I stored my heart of return and reverently awaited the good moment.

units.zh: 臣十月十日，決計殺在城契丹，取十一日離州，押七八千車乘，領十五萬生靈，十四日已達幽州」云。
units.en: On the tenth day of the tenth month I resolved to kill the Khitan in the city. On the eleventh I left the prefecture with seven or eight thousand carts and a hundred and fifty thousand people. On the fourteenth I reached Youzhou," he wrote.
units.literal: Your servant on the tenth day of the tenth month resolved to kill the Khitan in the city, on the eleventh left the prefecture, escorted seven or eight thousand carts, led a hundred and fifty thousand souls, and on the fourteenth had already reached Youzhou," he said.

units.zh: 洎至洛陽，明宗寵待彌厚，授滑州節度使、檢校太尉。
units.en: When he reached Luoyang, Mingzong treated him with exceptional favor and made him military governor of Huazhou and acting Grand Commandant.
units.literal: When he reached Luoyang, Mingzong favored and treated him ever more generously, appointing him military governor of Huazhou and acting Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 歲餘，移鎮鄧州，累加同平章事，入為上將軍。
units.en: After a year he was transferred to Deng Prefecture, made Associate Grand Councillor, and appointed Grand General at court.
units.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to govern Deng Prefecture, was repeatedly given the title of Associate Grand Councillor, and entered office as Grand General.

units.zh: 長興中，復出鎮潞州，擒奸恤隱，甚獲當時之譽。
