units.en: During the Changxing reign he returned to govern Lu Prefecture, where he punished the wicked and comforted the oppressed and won great praise.
units.literal: In the Changxing era he again went out to govern Lu Prefecture, seized the wicked and comforted the hidden, and won great praise in his day.

units.zh: 清泰中，改安州節度使。
units.en: During the Qingtai reign he was made military governor of An Prefecture.
units.literal: In the Qingtai era he was changed to military governor of An Prefecture.

units.zh: 及高祖即位，與契丹敦好，文進以嘗背契丹，居不自安。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne and made peace with the Khitan, Wenjin, who had once betrayed them, grew uneasy.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne and cultivated close relations with the Khitan, Wenjin, because he had once betrayed the Khitan, could not feel at ease in his post.

units.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書》：文進居數鎮，頗有善政，兵民愛之。
units.en: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang records that Wenjin governed several commands well and was loved by troops and people alike.
units.literal: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang: Wenjin held several commands and had rather good government; soldiers and people loved him.

units.zh: 其將行也，從數騎至營中，別其裨將李藏機，告以避契丹之意，將士皆拜為訣。）〉
units.en: When he prepared to leave, he rode with a few men to camp, bade farewell to his lieutenant Li Cangji, explained his plan to flee the Khitan, and the officers and soldiers all bowed in parting.)〉
units.literal: When he was about to leave, with several riders he came to camp, took leave of his lieutenant Li Cangji, told him of his intent to avoid the Khitan, and the officers and soldiers all bowed in farewell.)〉

units.zh: 天福元年十二月，乃殺行軍司馬馮知兆、節度副使杜重貴等，率其部眾渡淮奔於金陵。
units.en: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianfu he killed army marching marshal Feng Zhizhao, deputy military governor Du Chonggui, and others, led his followers across the Huai, and fled to Jinling.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianfu he killed the army marching marshal Feng Zhizhao, the deputy military governor Du Chonggui, and others, led his followers across the Huai, and fled to Jinling.

units.zh: 李棨待之尤重，
units.en: Li Qi treated him with exceptional honor,
units.literal: Li Qi treated him with especial weight,

units.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書》云：烈祖以文進為天雄統軍。）〉
units.en: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang says Liezu made Wenjin commander of the Tianxiong army.)〉
units.literal: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang says: Liezu made Wenjin commander of the Tianxiong army.)〉

units.zh: 偽命為宣州節度使，後卒於江南。
units.en: The southern regime appointed him military governor of Xuan Prefecture, and he later died in the south.
units.literal: by the false regime he was appointed military governor of Xuan Prefecture and later died in Jiangnan.

units.zh: 〈（《金陵志》：文進自潤州召還，以左衛上將軍、兼中書令、范陽郡王奉朝請。）〉
units.en: (Records of Jinling records that Wenjin was recalled from Run Prefecture and made Left Guard Grand General, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Fanyang attending court.)〉
units.literal: (Records of Jinling: Wenjin was recalled from Run Prefecture and made Left Guard Grand General, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Fanyang attending court.)〉

units.zh: 李金全，本唐明宗之小豎也。
units.en: Li Jinquan had originally been a young attendant to Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang.
units.literal: Li Jinquan was originally a young attendant of Tang Emperor Mingzong.

units.zh: 其先出於吐谷渾。
units.en: His ancestors were Tuyuhun.
units.literal: His ancestors came from the Tuyuhun.

units.zh: 金全驍勇，善騎射，少從明宗征伐，以力戰有功，明宗即位，連典大郡。
units.en: Jinquan was fierce and skilled in horsemanship and archery. He followed Mingzong on campaigns from youth and distinguished himself in battle. When Mingzong took the throne he governed several major prefectures in succession.
units.literal: Jinquan was fierce and brave, skilled in horsemanship and archery; in youth he followed Mingzong on campaigns and had merit through hard fighting; when Mingzong took the throne he successively governed great prefectures.

units.zh: 天成中，授涇州節度使，在鎮數年，以掊斂為務。
units.en: During the Tiancheng reign he was made military governor of Jing Prefecture, where for several years he devoted himself to extortion.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was appointed military governor of Jing Prefecture; during several years in his command he made extortion his business.

units.zh: 長興中，受代歸闕，始進馬數十匹，不數日又進之。
units.en: During the Changxing reign he was relieved and returned to court. He first presented several dozen horses, then within days presented more.
units.literal: In the Changxing era he was relieved and returned to court; he first presented several dozen horses, and within a few days presented them again.

units.zh: 明宗召而謂之曰：「卿患馬多耶，何進貢之數也？」
units.en: Mingzong summoned him and said, "Do you have too many horses? Why so many tribute presentations?"
units.literal: Mingzong summoned him and said, "Do you suffer from too many horses? Why so many tribute presentations?"

units.zh: 又謂曰：「卿在涇州日，為理如何，無乃以馬為事否？」
units.en: He also asked, "When you were at Jing Prefecture, how did you govern? Surely you did not make horses your only business?"
units.literal: He also said, "When you were at Jing Prefecture, how was your governance—surely you did not make horses your only business?"

units.zh: 金全慚謝而退。
units.en: Jinquan withdrew in shame.
units.literal: Jinquan withdrew in shame and thanks.

units.zh: 四年夏，授滄州節度使，累官至檢校太傅。
units.en: In the summer of the fourth year he was made military governor of Cang Prefecture and rose to acting Grand Tutor.
units.literal: In the fourth year, summer, he was appointed military governor of Cang Prefecture and rose in office to acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 清泰中，罷鎮歸闕，久留於京師。
units.en: During the Qingtai reign he left his command and returned to court, where he remained for a long time.
units.literal: In the Qingtai era he was removed from his command and returned to court, remaining long in the capital.

units.zh: 高祖即位之明年，安州屯將王暉殺節度使周瑰，詔遣金全以騎兵千人鎮撫其地。
units.en: The year after Gaozu took the throne, An Prefecture garrison officer Wang Hui killed military governor Zhou Gui. Gaozu ordered Jinquan to the region with a thousand cavalry to restore order.
units.literal: In the year after the High Ancestor took the throne, the An Prefecture garrison officer Wang Hui killed the military governor Zhou Gui; by edict Jinquan was sent with a thousand cavalry to pacify the region.

units.zh: 未及境，而暉為部下所殺。
units.en: Before Jinquan reached the prefecture, Hui was killed by his own men.
units.literal: Before he reached the border, Hui was killed by his subordinates.

units.zh: 金全至，亂軍數百人皆不安，金全說遣赴闕，密伏兵於野，盡殺之，又擒其軍校武彥和等數十人，斬之。
units.en: When Jinquan arrived, several hundred mutineers were uneasy. He persuaded them to go to court, then ambushed and killed them all. He also seized dozens of their officers including Wu Yanhe and beheaded them.
units.literal: When Jinquan arrived, several hundred men of the mutinous army were all uneasy; Jinquan persuaded them to go to court, secretly set ambush troops in the wild, and killed them all; he also seized their military officers Wu Yanhe and several dozen others and beheaded them.

units.zh: 初，金全之將行也，高祖戒之曰：「王暉之亂，罪莫大焉，但慮封守不寧，則民受其弊。」
units.en: Before Jinquan departed, Gaozu warned him: "Wang Hui's crime is grave, but I fear that if the frontier is unsettled the people will suffer."
units.literal: At first, when Jinquan was about to depart, the High Ancestor admonished him, saying, "Wang Hui's rebellion is a crime without equal, yet I fear that if the frontier is not settled the people will suffer harm."

units.zh: 因折矢飛詔，約以不戮一人，仍許以暉為唐州刺史。
units.en: He broke an arrow and sent an urgent edict pledging not to execute a single man and promising Hui the post of prefect of Tang Prefecture.
units.literal: He therefore broke an arrow and sent a flying edict, pledging not to execute a single man and still promising Hui the post of prefect of Tang Prefecture.

units.zh: 又謂金全曰：「卿之此行，無失吾信。」
units.en: He also told Jinquan, "On this mission, do not betray my word."
units.literal: He also told Jinquan, "On this mission of yours, do not betray my faith."

units.zh: 及金全至，聞彥和等當為亂之日，劫掠郡城，所獲財貨，悉在其第，遂殺而奪之。
units.en: When Jinquan arrived, he learned that on the day of the mutiny Yanhe and the others had plundered the city and stored the loot in their homes. He killed them and seized their goods.
units.literal: When Jinquan arrived, he heard that on the day Yanhe and the others had mutinied they had plundered the prefectural city and that all goods obtained were in their residences; he therefore killed them and seized the goods.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：彥和且死，呼曰：「王暉首惡，天子猶赦之；
units.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records that as Yanhe was about to die he cried out, "Wang Hui was the chief culprit, yet the emperor still pardoned him;
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: As Yanhe was about to die he cried out, "Wang Hui was the chief culprit, yet the Son of Heaven still pardoned him;

units.zh: 我輩脅從，何罪乎！」）〉
units.en: we were only coerced followers—what crime is ours!")〉
units.literal: we were coerced followers—what crime is ours!")〉

units.zh: 高祖聞之，以姑息金全故，不究其事，尋授以旄節。
units.en: When Gaozu heard of it he did not investigate, wishing to indulge Jinquan, and soon granted him a full military commission.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor heard of it, because he wished to indulge Jinquan he did not investigate the matter and soon granted him the military commission.

units.zh: 金全有親吏胡漢筠者，勇譎嗇褊，貪詐殘忍，軍府之政，一以委之。
units.en: Jinquan had a personal clerk named Hu Hanyun who was brave, cunning, stingy, greedy, deceitful, and cruel. He entrusted all military government affairs to him.
units.literal: Jinquan had a personal clerk named Hu Hanyun, brave, cunning, stingy, and narrow; greedy, deceitful, and cruel; military government affairs were wholly entrusted to him.

units.zh: 高祖聞其事，遣吏賈仁紹往代其職，且召漢筠。
units.en: When Gaozu heard of this he sent Jia Renshao to replace Hanyun and summoned Hanyun to court.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor heard of this he sent the official Jia Renshao to replace him in his duties and also summoned Hanyun.

units.zh: 漢筠內疚惶怖，金全乃列狀稱疾以聞。
units.en: Hanyun was consumed with guilt and fear. Jinquan memorialized claiming illness.
units.literal: Hanyun felt inner guilt and terror; Jinquan then submitted a memorial listing illness to report.

units.zh: 及仁紹至，漢筠鴆而殺之。
units.en: When Renshao arrived, Hanyun poisoned and killed him.
units.literal: When Renshao arrived, Hanyun poisoned and killed him.

units.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書》：胡漢榮所為多不法，晉高祖患之，不欲因漢榮以累功臣，為選廉吏賈仁沼代之，且召漢榮。
units.en: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang records that Hu Hanrong's conduct was largely unlawful. Gaozu was troubled but did not wish to implicate a meritorious minister; he selected the honest official Jia Renzhao to replace him and summoned Hanrong.
units.literal: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang: Hu Hanrong's conduct was largely unlawful; Jin High Ancestor was troubled by it and did not wish to implicate a meritorious minister because of Hanrong; he selected the honest official Jia Renzhao to replace him and also summoned Hanrong.

units.zh: 漢榮教金全留己而不遣。
units.en: Hanrong persuaded Jinquan to keep him and refuse to send him away.
units.literal: Hanrong taught Jinquan to keep him and not send him away.

units.zh: 金全客龐令圖諫曰：「仁沼昔事王晏球，有大功，晏球欲厚賞之，仁沼退而不言，此天下之忠臣也。
units.en: Jinquan's adviser Pang Lingtu remonstrated: "Renzhao once served Wang Yanqiu with great merit. When Yanqiu wished to reward him generously, Renzhao withdrew without a word. That is the loyalty of a true minister.
units.literal: Jinquan's guest Pang Lingtu remonstrated, saying, "Renzhao once served Wang Yanqiu and had great merit; Yanqiu wished to reward him generously, but Renzhao withdrew and said nothing—this is a loyal minister under Heaven.

units.zh: 及頒賜所俘物，仁沼悉以分故人親戚之貧者，此天下之廉士也。
units.en: When distributing captured goods he gave them all to old friends and poor relatives. That is the integrity of a true gentleman.
units.literal: When distributing captured goods, Renzhao gave them all to old friends and poor relatives—this is an honest man under Heaven.

units.zh: 宜納仁沼而遣漢榮。」
units.en: You should accept Renzhao and send Hanrong away."
units.literal: You should accept Renzhao and send Hanrong away."

units.zh: 漢榮聞之，夜使人殺令圖而鴆仁沼。）〉
units.en: When Hanrong heard of this he sent men in the night to kill Lingtu and poison Renzhao.)〉
units.literal: When Hanrong heard of this, in the night he sent men to kill Lingtu and poison Renzhao.)〉

units.zh: 天福五年夏，高祖命馬全節為安州節度使，以代金全。
units.en: In the summer of the fifth year of Tianfu Gaozu ordered Ma Quanjie to replace Jinquan as military governor of An Prefecture.
units.literal: In the summer of the fifth year of Tianfu the High Ancestor ordered Ma Quanjie to be military governor of An Prefecture to replace Jinquan.

units.zh: 漢筠自以昔嘗拒命，復聞仁紹二子將訴置毒之事，居不自安，乃紿謂金全曰：「邸吏劉珂使健步倍道兼行，密傳其意，雲受代之後，朝廷將以仁紹之事詰公之罪。」
units.en: Hanyun, having once defied orders and hearing that Renshao's two sons would sue over the poisoning, grew uneasy. He deceived Jinquan, saying, "Residence clerk Liu Ke sent a swift courier with a secret message that after you are replaced the court will prosecute you for the Renshao affair."
units.literal: Hanyun, because he had once defied orders and also heard that Renshao's two sons would sue over the poisoning affair, could not feel at ease; he therefore deceived Jinquan, saying, "The residence clerk Liu Ke sent a swift courier by double marches, secretly conveying his meaning, that after you are replaced the court will use the Renshao affair to question your guilt."

units.zh: 金全大駭，命從事張緯函表送款於淮夷。
units.en: Jinquan was terrified and ordered his aide Zhang Wei to send a sealed memorial of submission to the southern regime.
units.literal: Jinquan was greatly terrified and ordered his aide Zhang Wei to seal a memorial and send submission to the Huai barbarians.

units.zh: 淮人遣偽將李承裕以代金全，金全即日南竄，其妓樂、車馬、珍奇、帑藏，皆為承裕所奪。
units.en: The southerners sent their general Li Chengyu to replace him. Jinquan fled south that same day. Chengyu seized his entertainers, horses, carriages, treasures, and treasury stores.
units.literal: The Huai people sent the false general Li Chengyu to replace Jinquan; Jinquan fled south that very day; his entertainers, horses and carriages, rare objects, and treasury stores were all seized by Chengyu.

units.zh: 與其黨數百人束身夜出，曉至汊州，引領北望，泣下而去。
units.en: With several hundred followers he fled by night. At dawn he reached Chazhou, gazed north with tears, and went on.
units.literal: With several hundred of his faction he bound himself and went out by night; at dawn he reached Chazhou, stretched his neck looking north, wept, and departed.

units.zh: 及至金陵，李棨授以節鎮。
units.en: When he reached Jinling, Li Qi granted him a military commission.
units.literal: When he reached Jinling, Li Qi granted him a military commission.

units.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書》云：烈祖以金全為天威統軍，遷潤州節度使。）〉
units.en: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang says Liezu made Jinquan commander of the Tianwei army and military governor of Run Prefecture.)〉
units.literal: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang says: Liezu made Jinquan commander of the Tianwei army and transferred him to military governor of Run Prefecture.)〉

units.zh: 後卒於江南。
units.en: He later died in the south.
units.literal: He later died in Jiangnan.

units.zh: 史臣曰：延光昔為唐臣，綽有令譽，洎逢晉祚，顯恣狂謀，既力屈以來降，尚顏而惜死，孟津之歿，乃取笑於千載也。
units.en: The historian writes: Yanguang was once a Tang minister of fine reputation. Under the Jin he openly plotted rebellion. Though defeated and forced to surrender, he clung to life and face. His death at the Meng Ford crossing will be mocked for a thousand years.
units.literal: The historian says: Yanguang was once a Tang minister and had ample fair renown; when he met the Jin fortune he openly indulged mad schemes; though his strength was spent and he came to surrender, he still clung to face and cherished life—the death at Meng Ford will be laughed at for a thousand years.

units.zh: 從賓而下，俱怙亂以滅身，亦何足與議也。
units.en: Congbin and those below all courted rebellion and destroyed themselves. They are hardly worth discussing.
units.literal: Congbin and those below him all relied on disorder to destroy themselves—what is there worth discussing?

units.zh: 文進懼強敵之威，金全為輿臺所賣，事雖弗類，叛則攸同，鹹附島夷，皆可醜也。
units.en: Wenjin fled from a powerful enemy; Jinquan was betrayed by his own attendants. Their cases differ, but in rebellion they were alike. Both threw in their lot with southern regimes. Both deserve contempt.
units.literal: Wenjin feared the might of a strong enemy; Jinquan was sold out by his attendants; though the affairs were not alike, in rebellion they were the same—all clinging to island barbarians, all may be held contemptible.
